Outbreak of Norovirus Disrupts Media & Publishing Workforces Across Guernsey

Media and publishing firms across Guernsey are facing significant disruption following an outbreak of norovirus at multiple company sites this week. As of Thursday, more than 60 staff members from at least five publishing houses and local newsrooms are confirmed to be affected, according to statements from the Guernsey Media Industry Association (GMIA).

Symptoms of the highly contagious virus, including vomiting and diarrhea, first appeared among editorial and print staff at the St. Peter Port production facility of Island Printworks on Monday. By Wednesday, similar cases were reported at the offices of Guernsey Press House and the headquarters of Channel Magazines Ltd.

“Several teams have been operating at reduced capacity since the outbreak began,” said GMIA spokesperson Maxine Jory. “Editorial deadlines have proved challenging, and some print runs are delayed by up to 36 hours. We are working closely with public health officials to minimize further spread.”

Affected sites have implemented deep-cleaning regimes, and remote working policies have been expanded, especially for journalists and design staff. However, production and distribution teams have found it more difficult to shift their work offsite, leading to missed publication schedules and a backlog at several print facilities, according to union representatives.

“We’re prioritizing staff well-being, but the knock-on effects for weekly and daily titles are real,” said Isla de Carteret, HR manager at a local publishing house. “Freelancers and temporary workers have been brought in to help cover shifts, but the situation remains fluid.”

The GMIA estimates that at least 20% of the Guernsey-based media and publishing workforce is currently either unwell or self-isolating. Industry leaders are urging all employees to report symptoms promptly and continue following enhanced hygiene protocols until the outbreak subsides.
